content.title: About
content.content: Summer squash (Cucurbita pepo) is the immature fruit of the zucchini plant, harvested while still tender. It is available in yellow or green varieties and can be eaten raw or cooked. When prepared, a small amount of fat (oil or butter) is often added to enhance flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Summer squash belongs to the cucurbit family, which also includes pumpkins, cucumbers, and melons.
Unlike many other squashes, it can be enjoyed raw, offering a crisp and mild taste.
The yellow hue comes from the natural pigment xanthophyll.
It is a staple in many world cuisines, from Italian ratatouille to Asian stir‑fries.
Fresh summer squash is very low in calories—about 17 kcal per 100 g.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low calorie content
items.content: Ideal for energy‑restricted diets and weight management.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart function.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect eye health and combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to cucurbit vegetables.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic squash, wash thoroughly to reduce residue exposure.

items.title: Excess fat during cooking
items.content: Using too much added oil increases the dish’s calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Summer squash can be sliced raw into salads, spiralized into “zoodles,” baked, sautéed, grilled, or steamed. When cooking, add 1‑2 tsp of oil to improve flavor and prevent sticking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store squash in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a perforated bag. It stays fresh for up to 5 days. Keep it away from ethylene‑producing fruits to slow ripening.
